geometry_edits.rationale: Reduce the overly repetitive step count while preserving the dominant stepped bar gesture.
Soften the tiering so the silhouette reads as continuous inhabited terraces rather than generic stair-steps.
Expand the carved void to make a more usable public court at the ground threshold.
Orient the public opening to the verified access edge.

graph_edits.rationale: Retarget the dominant mass from a generic setback stack to a more spatially continuous stepped envelope so the section reads as one legible rule rather than repeated tiering.
Increase the sectional legibility slightly while keeping the dominant gesture compact.
Reduce the stair-like aggressiveness of the stepping so the silhouette resolves as a capacity-bearing inhabited terrace rather than code-minimum tiering.
Widen the courtyard/notch so the void becomes legible as public ground rather than a sliver.
Keep the public threshold aligned to the verified access side specified by the program frame.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent stepped bar in some views, but it is not yet convincing as a neighborhood-living massing. The dominant gesture is recognizable, yet the form feels mechanically tiered rather than spatially purposeful. The courtyard/notch logic is present in plan, but the void is too thin and semantically weak to count as a strong public threshold. Most importantly, the verified road frontage/access edge is met with a largely sealed side; the public response does not clearly align with the access condition. Across views, the mass stays mostly one family, so there is no catastrophic view conflict, but the section remains shallow and generic for the brief. Overall this is a plausible early mass study, not a program-fit solution.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is much lower and more bar-like; it lacks the tower-like vertical emphasis and urban skyline role of the reference.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped upper massing with a clear dominant datum and a legible tapered/offset profile can support mixed-use presence.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is predominantly a tower; the candidate's low stepped bar does not share the same typological scale or section logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A tall mass can use a controlled setback and softened vertical profile to keep hierarchy while changing silhouette.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is a small low-rise pavilion; its simplicity is useful, but the candidate still needs a clearer street-side opening and public void.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: An active ground threshold and a modest public-facing edge response matter more than an elaborate roof shape for neighborhood-serving programs.

warnings: Verified access edge appears to be answered weakly or on the wrong side.
Public void is too narrow to read as a usable neighborhood threshold.
The stepped silhouette is coherent, but it risks reading as repetitive setback code rather than a program-led section.
